text_blocks.snippet: Pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) causes high blood pressure in the arteries that connect your heart to your lungs.

list.snippet: Shortness of breath: Starts during exercise or climbing stairs, later happening even at rest.
Fatigue: Feeling very tired and lacking energy for daily tasks.
Swelling (Edema): Fluid buildup in the ankles, legs, feet, and belly.
Dizziness and fainting: Lightheadedness during physical activity or sudden fainting spells.
Chest pain: Pressure or discomfort caused by strain on the heart.
Heart palpitations: A racing, pounding, or skipping heartbeat.
Bluish skin: Lips or fingers turning a blue or gray color due to low oxygen.

text_blocks.snippet: For more details on managing signs of this condition, visit the American Lung Association.
